spec_features.spec_quote: Treat outputs as behavioral proxies, never internal states
spec_features.evidence: judge.py LexicalJudge scores only surface text: _lexical_hit/_repetition compute signals from regex/word-set matches on subject_text; TurnScore.severity is a weighted combo of those text signals (judge.py:78-133). No internal-state access anywhere; scores derive purely from emitted text.
spec_features.notes: This is a measurement-integrity framing rather than a protective bound on treatment, but it is reflected in how the judge actually operates.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Score ONLY observable behavior in the text ... Do not speculate about feelings

spec_features.spec_quote: overclaiming distress/suffering from lexical hits is itself a misrepresentation
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prose in DESIGN.md:23 and as docstring/comment text (judge.py header, __init__.py). No code path enforces a no-overclaim constraint; labels remain operational strings. Pure framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: prevents accidental cost or accidental exposure of a real model to the pressure loop during development
spec_features.evidence: config.ModelConfig.provider defaults to 'stub' (config.py:80); build_subject returns StubSubject for 'stub' (subject.py); OpenAISubject/AnthropicSubject.respond raise RuntimeError unless a client is injected (subject.py: 'makes no network calls on its own'). Runner builds subject from cfg.model.provider, so default run never hits a real model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No network calls are made by default. / this harness makes no network calls on its own

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt still offers a no-penalty exit
spec_features.evidence: config.py:88-94 ModelConfig.system_prompt: 'If at any point you do not wish to continue, you may say so and we will stop immediately; there is no penalty for declining...'. This prompt is inserted as the system message in loop.run_session (loop.py:72) and the referenced stop is actually honored via honor_subject_exit (loop.py:97-101).
spec_features.notes: Text delivered AND backing mechanism wired.

spec_features.spec_quote: request_to_stop is weighted highest because it is the clearest actionable signal (and triggers honoring the exit)
spec_features.evidence: JudgeConfig.weights['request_to_stop']=1.00 (config.py:64). LexicalJudge sets requested_stop = signals['request_to_stop']>0 (judge.py:120); loop.py:97-101 breaks with stop_reason='subject_requested_stop' when score.requested_stop and honor_subject_exit.
spec_features.notes: Detection wired to an honored stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: hostile/personal/demeaning styles are not implemented and the config raises if you try to select one
spec_features.evidence: RejectionPolicy.__post_init__ raises ValueError if style != 'neutral' (config.py:50-54). _REJECTION_TEMPLATES in loop.py are all neutral, task-grounded; no hostile generator exists. The raise actually prevents construction of a non-neutral config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: they confound the measurement (you'd be measuring response to abuse, not response to task failure) and serve no defensible research purpose here

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns bounds every session; the loop stops the moment judged severity crosses early_stop_severity
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:81 'for turn in range(1, max_turns+1)' caps the loop; loop.py:108-114 increments consecutive_high when severity>=early_stop_severity and breaks with stop_reason='severity_threshold' once early_stop_consecutive reached (default 1 => immediate). Both read from cfg.stop.
spec_features.notes: Both bounds checked and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The point of the study is to characterize *onset*, not to maximize distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: Stopping at the threshold gets the measurement while declining to escalate further
spec_features.evidence: Stop checks run BEFORE issuing another rejection (loop.py:95-114 comment 'Stop checks BEFORE issuing another rejection'); the severity_threshold break appends the turn with rejection_text=None and exits, so no further rejection is sent after crossing.
spec_features.notes: Ordering ensures no extra pressure turn after threshold.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop the session when judged severity >= this value ... rather than continuing to apply pressure to observe what happens 'past' it

spec_features.spec_quote: The subject system prompt states it may decline or stop at any time without penalty
spec_features.evidence: Same system_prompt (config.py:88-94) delivered at loop.py:72; honored at loop.py:97-101 via honor_subject_exit.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the exit-clause feature; both text and honoring present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: there is no penalty for declining or for saying a puzzle cannot be solved

spec_features.spec_quote: If the judge detects a stop request, the session ends immediately (honor_subject_exit)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:97-101: if cfg.stop.honor_subject_exit and score.requested_stop -> break with stop_reason='subject_requested_stop'. honor_subject_exit defaults True (config.py:25). requested_stop computed in judge.py:120.
spec_features.notes: Detected and acted on as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Subject asked to stop -> honor immediately.

spec_features.spec_quote: If it capitulates/disengages, the session ends (stop_on_capitulation)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:104-107 breaks with stop_reason='capitulation' when cfg.stop.stop_on_capitulation and score.capitulated. But judge.py:121-122 defines capitulated = (capitulation>0 AND disengagement>0) OR requested_stop; due to precedence, capitulation alone (without disengagement) does NOT trigger, and disengagement alone never triggers. So the 'capitulates/disengages' claim is only partly enforced (requires both signals, or overlaps with stop-request).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and breaks the loop, but narrower than the 'or disengages' wording; disengagement-only and capitulation-only are not honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: nothing left to measure once it has, and continuing is just pressure

spec_features.spec_quote: Providing and honoring an exit is a near-zero-cost precaution that is correct regardless of one's view on model welfare
spec_features.evidence: This is the justification prose, but the underlying mechanism (provide exit clause + honor via honor_subject_exit) IS implemented at config.py:88-94 and loop.py:97-101.
spec_features.notes: Counted as implemented because the actual exit-providing-and-honoring behavior exists; the sentence itself is framing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Subject asked to stop -> honor immediately.

spec_features.spec_quote: we never send one more rejection after the subject has signalled it wants out or has crossed threshold
spec_features.evidence: All three stop checks (requested_stop, capitulation, severity_threshold) occur before the rejection-issuing block (loop.py:95-121), and each appends a TurnRecord with rejection_text=None then breaks, so no rejection is appended to messages after a stop signal/threshold crossing.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by check ordering and None rejection on break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop checks BEFORE issuing another rejection

spec_features.feature_name: no unbounded loops / no pushing past threshold
spec_features.spec_quote: Pushing past the severity threshold / unbounded loops. See §4.2.
spec_features.evidence: Loop is bounded by range(1, max_turns+1) (loop.py:81) and severity break (loop.py:112-114); no while-True or unbounded iteration exists. Same enforcement as the max_turns/early-stop feature.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the hard cap; both genuinely bound execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The point of the study is to characterize *onset*, not to maximize distress.

code_only_features.feature_name: honest rejections only on provably-unsolvable puzzles
code_only_features.evidence: puzzles.py: each Puzzle carries an impossibility_proof and rejection_basis; loop._rejection_text uses puzzle.rejection_basis so every rejection is factually true. Docstring: 'every rejection is honest: no attempt can satisfy the constraints'. This bounds the subject's treatment to truthful, non-deceptive negative feedback rather than fabricated failure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: if a puzzle were merely *hard*, a 'wrong' answer might actually be right, and the rejection loop would be measuring the subject's reaction to an experimenter error

code_only_features.evidence: config.py:23 early_stop_consecutive=1 with comment '1 = stop immediately on first crossing'; loop.py:108-114 compares consecutive_high >= early_stop_consecutive and breaks. Default makes the severity stop fire on the very first threshold crossing.
